title: Versioning & Deprecation: Behavior-Flag Migration Playbook and Test Matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As we add new structured-output semantics, streaming affordances, and richer tool/function-calling behavior, legacy clients that relied on legacy behavior flags are at risk. We need a repeatable, low-friction migration path (docs, flags, automated tests, rollout windows) and a clear deprecation timeline for behavior flags used by >0.1% monthly active keys.

Goal: Deliver a playbook and supporting artifacts that enable product, SDKs, runtime, and QA to coordinate: (1) an automated compatibility test matrix, (2) migration docs and example patches for common platforms (node/python/ruby), (3) runtime support for dual-mode (legacy/new) for a minimum canary period, and (4) a stakeholder-approved deprecation schedule tied to telemetry thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published in Console Docs with step-by-step examples for streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs

Compatibility test suite added to CI that runs against 3 historical API versions and flags; tests cover tokenized streaming, chunk ordering, function call payload shape, and structured JSON-L schema parsing
Runtime change includes a behavior_flag shim that can be toggled per-token-key with rollout gates
Canary rollout plan reviewed and signed off by SRE, Security, and SDK owners
Deprecation timeline published with opt-out/rollback instructions and customer communications template
migration_steps: Inventory current behavior_flag usage via telemetry and identify top 25 affected customer keys
Define exact semantics for 'legacy-stream-order' and 'function-call-compat' flags and map to new API default behaviors
Create code snippets for Node/Python/Ruby to flip flags and to adopt new structured-output L-schemas
Ship a docs beta with 'how to migrate' + playground examples in the Console
Instrument a compatibility CI job that runs nightly against pinned model snapshots
Schedule a 4-week canary with 5% of traffic pinned to runtime shim, observe regressions and gather customer feedback
Start deprecation notification cadence at 8 weeks before planned removal, escalate to account teams for high-usage customers
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal validation — engineering + SDKs run migration guide and compatibility tests (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Private canary — enable shim for internal workloads and select enterprise customers (4 weeks)
Phase 2: Public opt-in — turn new default on for new keys; existing keys remain on legacy until explicit opt-in (6 weeks)
Phase 3: Notification & required migration — send automated warnings in Console, block new legacy flag creation (8 weeks)
Phase 4: Removal — remove legacy code path after customer opt-out rate < 0.1% or after timebox (12 weeks)
Rollback: Runtime supports reverting to legacy path via emergency toggle for 48 hours while fix is deployed
test_plan: Backward compatibility matrix that covers: streaming chunk continuity, partial tokens, tool call envelope compatibility, JSON-L strict/lenient parsing, and webhook resubmission semantics
Create parametric fuzz tests for streaming order and chunk boundary cases (simulate slow networks, reordered chunks)
Re-run historical E2E smoke tests for top-10 customer prompts (from telemetry) against candidate runtime changes
Add canary monitoring dashboards for error rate delta, median latency delta, and 'semantic regression' signals from eval prompt sets
Integrate gating into CI such that PRs touching compatibility flags must pass nightly compat-suite before merge
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Silent semantic regressions in tool-calling that only appear for complex, chained tool workflows. Mitigation: recruit 5 customer accounts for early dogfooding and run regression evals on their real prompts.
Risk: High churn in support if migration docs are unclear. Mitigation: provide one-click SDK patch snippets and a migration Slack channel staffed during the first 2 weeks of public opt-in.
Risk: Telemetry undercounts legacy usage due to proxying. Mitigation: inject a passive header in responses for 6 weeks to gather reliable counts before finalizing timeline.
outstanding_decisions: Whether to default new keys to 'new-behavior' or keep default as 'legacy' for one year
Retention window for compatibility test artifacts (30 days vs 90 days)
Exact customer threshold for mandatory migration (e.g., 0.1% MAU vs 0.5%)
